definition: Garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about unimportant things.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word garrulous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know garrulous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The garrulous ranger turned a ten-minute trailhead briefing into an hour on squirrel politics and the full history of his hat.
Chatty is far milder than garrulous — chatty company makes a pleasant hour, and nobody reaches for their headphones.
Long-winded comes closer but still stops short of garrulous — a long-winded speaker takes too long to make a point, while a garrulous one keeps talking after the points have run out.

Gabby is the light, affectionate word for someone who talks a lot — the friendly neighbor who keeps you at the fence a few minutes too long. Garrulous is the heavyweight charge: talk that runs long past anyone's patience, mostly about trivia. Gabby teases; garrulous condemns.

Rambling describes the path of the talk — wandering from topic to topic without direction — and even a short answer can ramble. Garrulous describes the person and the sheer quantity: too much talk, too little matter, going on long after every listener has given up.
deliberately saying as little as possible

Latin garrire ('to chatter') imitated the sound of babble, and it left English no other common descendant — garrulous stands alone. The garr- you might spot in 'garrison' is unrelated; that one comes from an old French word for defense and protection.
Garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about unimportant things.

Seat 14C taught Mira a lesson about red-eye flights: her garrulous seatmate narrated his fantasy-football roster, his sister's kitchen renovation, and the plot of a movie neither of them had seen, all before the drink cart reached row nine.
Garrulous is not a compliment: it means talkative past anyone's patience, usually about things that matter to no one else.
The garrulous talker doesn't exchange conversation — he supplies all of it, in bulk, on topics of his own choosing.
Garrulous criticizes: too much talk, too little matter.
Loquacious (also in this unit) can stay neutral or even admiring about a fluent talker; garrulous never does — it adds tedium and triviality to the volume.
The garrulous uncle isn't just talkative; he's still going, and it's about his lawn mower.
